item.title: Nacho Limits 0.1.2
item.description:
What's new

  • Nacho Limits can now update itself: right-click the notch and choose Check for Updates…, or use Settings > General.
  • The closed notch now says whose limit it is ("Max 98%"), not just a number.
  • Codex can be turned off in Settings > Providers.

Fixes

  • A fresh install no longer shows someone else's account names; your accounts appear under their own folder names, ready to rename.
  • The DeepSeek and NanoGPT key fields are visible again, and pasting a key works.
  • Hovering the notch no longer flashes the wide layout before it opens.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.1.3
item.description:
Fixes

  • The closed notch shows the full account name again ("Max 1h55m", not "Ma").
  • The installer window points to nacholimits.hexadexa.io.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.1.4
item.description:
• Glass mode is now readable over bright windows, in both the hover peek and the open panel.
  • Columns with no data (such as the 24 h graph) stay hidden until there is something to show, so the rest get the room.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.1.5
item.description:
What's new

  • Nacho moved into your notch: a tiny face on the left shows how your tightest limit is doing (calm, getting warm, sweating, out, napping after a reset). Prefer a ring or nothing? Settings > Display > Left side.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.0
item.description:
What's new

  • Knows when you'll run out, more honestly. Pace now follows your last hour of use, not the whole window's average, and shows a safe rate that lasts to the reset.
  • What to use next, in one click. "Most room" now counts the weekly limit too. Launch opens Claude Code on that account in Terminal (or iTerm); you can also copy the command.
  • Click any row for a 24-hour chart, burn rate, reset time and the last four weeks. Right-click to pin, hide, rename or launch.
  • Week view: which windows ran out, when you were close, your busiest hours, and a card to share.
  • More services: GitHub Copilot (premium requests), OpenRouter and Kimi are built in. Ready-made scripts add Anthropic and OpenAI API spend against a budget you set.
  • Outside the notch: desktop widgets, Spotlight and Shortcuts ("tightest limit", "which account has room"), and the `nacho` command for Terminal.
  • First run in the notch: Nacho walks you through connecting Claude Code.
  • Settings has tabs now, with a live preview of the closed notch and a shortcut you can change.
  • Nacho blinks, sweats and hops when a window resets, and says what the numbers mean. Settings > General turns his lines off.
  • Portuguese (Portugal).
  • Optional: mark Claude and OpenAI incidents from their public status pages (off by default).

Fixes

  • Clicking a notification opens the notch at that row. Alerts are silent unless you turn the sound on.
  • Problems are explained in plain words, with the button that fixes them.
  • Low-balance alerts compare each balance in its own currency.
  • Two identical monitors can be chosen separately.
  • Many accounts no longer get cut off: the panel scrolls.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.1
item.description:
Fixes

  • Nacho now hides over full-screen games, including borderless ones and games that take over the mouse. He comes back when you leave the game, and still shows if you push the pointer against the top edge.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.2
item.description:
What's new

  • Screens without a notch now get a menu-bar item: Nacho, your tightest limit with its countdown, and a small meter per Claude account. Click it and the panel drops down right under it, on that screen. Prefer it plain? Settings > Notch > Colourful menu bar item.
  • Choose where Nacho appears: MacBook screen only, all screens, or the screens you pick (Settings > Notch > Show on).

Fixes

  • Only one screen opens at a time: hovering or opening Nacho on one screen closes it on the other.
  • VoiceOver can open the panel from the menu-bar item.
  • Check for Updates always shows its window: it no longer opens hidden behind the app you're using, under the open notch, or not at all while a background check was running.
  • The floating pill under the menu bar is gone; the menu-bar item replaces it.
  • Opening Nacho Limits while another copy is running closes the other one, so it never shows twice.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.3
item.description:
What's new

  • Hide Nacho with a shortcut: ⌃⌥⌘N hides him from the notch and the menu bar, so the space next to the notch is free (for example for the menu bar's overflow arrow). Press it again to bring him back; opening Nacho Limits or the open shortcut (⌥⌘U) also does. Change it in Settings > General, or use Hide Nacho in the right-click menu.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.4
item.description:
What's new

  • Click Nacho: he tells a joke. Some are about your actual numbers ("Pro is going fast. Like me at a party."), some about the hour, most are just Nacho. Five quick clicks still get you rate-limited.
  • Nacho's birthday (30 October): a party hat, a few birthday lines, and one notification that day. Click him to hear why.
  • Your anniversary with Nacho: once a year, on the day you first opened the app, he says hi, with a short recap of the windows he watched for you.
  • Share card: on those days it wears the hat and carries the occasion.

Fixes

  • Turning off "Nacho's lines and surprises" now also hides the party hat, and stops the birthday and anniversary notifications.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.5
item.description:
What's new

  • What's new, after an update: when Nacho has updated himself, he says so once: "Updated to 0.2.5. Click me for what's new." One click opens the release notes; after that he's back to his usual lines.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.6
item.description:
Fixes

  • Settings fits each tab: the window grows to show everything on the tab instead of cutting it off (General no longer hides Updates). Only a tab taller than your screen scrolls.
  • Nacho's 5-hour break is a real break: after five quick clicks he only says the rate-limit line, ignores clicks until it's over, and then goes back to his usual line instead of repeating earlier jokes.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.7
item.description:
New

  • The closed countdown says what it counts: "Pro A out 20m" when you're on pace to run out, "↻ 1h55m" until a reset.
  • Account rings shows one ring per Claude account beside the notch, as the name says.
  • Hovering the notch suggests the account to use next when one is nearly out.
  • Settings > Alerts tells you when macOS notifications are off for Nacho Limits, links to the switch, and can send a test notification.
  • Keyboard: Tab moves between rows in the open panel; the right-click menu and the band's buttons show their shortcuts.
  • Reduce Transparency turns the glass panel solid.

Fixes

  • Portuguese: "Semana" no longer cuts off in Accounts, and the Week summary wraps instead of trailing off.
  • The open panel keeps one width when you switch views, and its scroll bar stays clear of the rounded corner.
  • Timeline labels for "out" and "reset" no longer overlap when they're close.
  • Clearer wording: "88% of its 5 h window left", old readings say how old they are everywhere, and an old Claude reading isn't shown in green in Settings.
  • Settings: API key captions sit on two tidy lines, the window title follows the tab, and the menu-bar colour option only shows when a menu-bar item exists.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.2.8
item.description:
Fixes

  • The open panel no longer scrolls when you open a row's details: it grows to fit the view, the details and Nacho's line, and only scrolls if your screen is too short.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.3.10
item.description:
New

  • Hovering over the notch can show the accounts you choose, in your order: Settings > Notch > On hover. The 3 tightest limits stay the default.
  • Claude account names stay with their Claude login. Settings > Accounts shows which account each Claude Code folder is signed into. If a folder is signed into another account, the name moves with that account, and numbers from the old login are dropped. A folder signed into the same account as another one is flagged instead of showing the same numbers twice.
  • `nacho tightest` and `nacho room` answer in one sentence: the limit closest to running out, and the Claude account with the most room.

Fixes

  • The open notch always closes with Esc or a click outside, including a click just below it, switching apps with ⌘-Tab, changing Spaces and when the screen sleeps.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.3.11
item.description:
Fixes

  • A plan reset shows up right away. Before, an account that had its limit reset kept showing the old percentage until the window ended. A Claude Code session that's sitting idle no longer puts an older number back either.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.3.12
item.description:
New

  • Gemini plan limits. If you use the Antigravity CLI (`agy`), open Settings > Accounts > Gemini and click Connect. Your 5-hour and weekly Gemini limits then show up next to the others while agy is open. agy keeps its own status line, and Disconnect puts everything back.

item.title: Nacho Limits 0.3.13
item.description:
New

  • The closed notch's right side can show nothing, like the left: Settings > Notch > Right side > Nothing.

Fixes

  • Settings > Accounts > Gemini says when it's still waiting for agy's first numbers: open agy, or restart a window that was already open.
